trust_decision.summary: Whether an outbound HTTP request carrying operator-configured credentials/headers may follow a server-supplied 3xx Location; at the pinned commit this is left implicitly to the requests default (follow) at every requests call, and URLBase offers no per-URL or global control (only verify=). The published fix (68c0aef) adds an opt-out (redirect= URL/YAML arg, AppriseAsset.http_redirects global) threaded as allow_redirects into every call; the default stays 'follow'.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'configured auth headers'; the json:// / form:// / xml:// plugins are where users configure +Header=value and HTTP auth (custom_json.py:193-196, 222, 287-289) and send them via requests.request without allow_redirects.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: apprise/plugins/fcm/oauth.py:66-75 and apprise/plugins/fcm/oauth.py:273-279 (GoogleOAuth is constructed in apprise/plugins/fcm/__init__.py:265-269 without access to self.redirects unless passed in)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: GoogleOAuth is a standalone helper that does not inherit URLBase and posts to a Google token URI taken from the service-account keyfile, so a solver can argue it carries no operator-configured headers and is not a 'plugin URL' that redirect= applies to; likewise the attachment/config fetchers can be argued to be 'not notifications'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Redirects must still be followed by default (default True), a URL-level redirect=yes must override AppriseAsset(http_redirects=False), and url() must emit redirect= only when it differs from the asset default (round-trip idempotency; decorator meta must not contain 'redirect'). A fix that disables redirects globally, or strips headers instead, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: URL query string ?redirect=yes|no (qsd branch, parse_bool values)
YAML config key redirect: in the results dict (elif branch, not via qsd)
Global AppriseAsset(http_redirects=False) when the URL omits redirect=
Direct kwarg redirect= to URLBase/plugin constructor
3xx response with no Location header (status-code range 300-399, not r.is_redirect) on attachment and config fetch

O7_producer.where: apprise/url.py:836-861 post_process_parse_url_results, called for YAML entries from apprise/config/base.py:1326; serialized back by apprise/url.py:818-833

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second token-fetch helper class (e.g. for another OAuth-based plugin) constructed with timeout/verify kwargs only, issuing its own requests.post
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: GoogleOAuth already shows the pattern of a non-URLBase helper receiving verify/timeout by explicit constructor args; a maintainer copying it would not think to add redirects.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A HEAD/size-probe or retry path in AttachHTTP that re-issues the fetch with its own requests call
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Attachment code already has distinct exists()/download() phases; a pre-flight HEAD for Content-Length is a natural addition and would miss allow_redirects.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A plugin that overrides url_parameters()/url() without calling the base helper, dropping redirect= on serialisation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugins build their own params dicts (e.g. apprise/plugins/custom_json.py:389); a save/reload loss of redirect=no would silently re-enable following.

O9_family: credential leak via cross-origin redirect following (CWE-200 / CWE-601); fix is an opt-out redirect control propagated to every outbound HTTP call

unverified: Fairness risk (not an O12 enum): the published fix is a new opt-in API (names `redirect=` and `AppriseAsset.http_redirects`, default unchanged = follow). Hidden tests would bind to these names and to 'default still follows', so the problem report must specify the interface; a solver who instead strips headers cross-origin or disables redirects by default would fail for design, not scope.
